text: so ok look here. see this magenta line i drew. [Image #7] that is the gap between me and the shelf for example, well. oddly enough if i look at the shelf in iso3d it has [Image #8] what looks to be the same exact amount of collision space as a ghost here.
resolution: Root cause: a prop placed in the iso build pane becomes a PlacedBuildPiece and collides via GAME_BUILD.placed.colliders, which lowers the build-catalog def.size. The catalog set a prop's size.depthMeters = footprintRadiusMeters*2 (a fat SQUARE) for any kind not hand-listed in PROP_DEPTH_OVERRIDES — and shelves weren't listed. So liquorShelf's collider was 1.8m deep while its model is ~0.5m, parking the player ~1m off the face (the magenta gap), and the iso pane drew that same fat footprint. The footprint was defined in THREE drifting tables (props.footprintRadius, world/props SEGMENT_HALF_THICKNESS, catalog PROP_DEPTH_OVERRIDES). Per the user's ruling I unified to ONE source: added a canonical footprintDepthMeters on each rectangular prop def (34 props, reconciled from SEGMENT*2 ∪ overrides), deleted both side tables, and wired catalog size + placement grid + world/props physics to read the def field (width derives from footprintRadiusMeters*2). Build-piece collision for shelves goes fat→thin (the fix); /test world.props physics for segment props is unchanged; signs/appliances gain a more-accurate thin oriented footprint. Verified: hmsc-int bundles clean and 7 suites pass (world/props, kinds/props, worldColliders, worldGeometry, worldParity, build, placed). NOT committed: the three edited files are mid-flight with a parallel session's untracked imported-props feature (props.ts imports untracked importedProps.generated.ts), so a clean isolated commit isn't possible without sweeping in or breaking that work — deferring commit sequencing to the supervisor.
